prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Decision Criteria Under Uncertainty
area.rationale: Candidates from two lessons cover the use of payoff tables and non-probabilistic decision criteria (Maximax, Maximin, Minimax Regret, Laplace, Hurwicz, Expected Value) along with decision environments. Together they teach the fundamentals of choosing among alternatives when outcomes are uncertain.

candidates.label: Payoff Table Structure
candidates.description: A payoff table organizes decision alternatives (rows) and states of nature (columns), with payoffs in cells representing outcomes.
coverage_criteria: Given a description, construct a payoff table.
Identify alternatives and states in a payoff table.

candidates.label: Maximax (Optimistic) Criterion
candidates.description: An optimistic approach: select the alternative with the best possible outcome. For profits, maximize the maximum; for costs, minimize the minimum.
coverage_criteria: Given a payoff table, apply the maximax criterion.
Explain the optimistic philosophy.

candidates.label: Maximin (Conservative) Criterion
candidates.description: A conservative approach: select the alternative with the best worst-case outcome. For profits, maximize the minimum; for costs, minimize the maximum.
coverage_criteria: Apply maximin to a payoff table.
Explain the conservative assumption.

candidates.label: Minimax Regret Criterion
candidates.description: A decision criterion that minimizes the maximum regret. Regret is the difference between the best possible payoff and the actual payoff for each state. The alternative with the smallest maximum regret is chosen.
coverage_criteria: Construct a regret table from a payoff table.
Apply the minimax regret criterion.

candidates.label: Laplace Criterion
candidates.description: A decision criterion that assumes all states of nature are equally likely and selects the alternative with the highest average payoff.
coverage_criteria: Apply the Laplace criterion to a payoff table.
Explain the equal likelihood assumption.

candidates.label: Hurwicz Criterion
candidates.description: A decision criterion that balances optimism and pessimism using a coefficient of optimism (α). It computes a weighted average of the best and worst payoffs for each alternative.
coverage_criteria: Calculate the Hurwicz value for given alternatives and α.
Explain how α reflects optimism.

candidates.label: Laplace Criterion (Equally Likely/Insufficient Reason)
candidates.description: Decision rule that assumes all states of nature are equally likely, computing the average payoff for each alternative and selecting the highest average.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the equally likely assumption
Student can calculate average payoffs from a payoff table
Student can determine the optimal alternative using this criterion

candidates.label: Hurwicz Criterion (Weighted Optimism/Pessimism)
candidates.description: Decision rule that balances best and worst payoffs using a coefficient of optimism α, computing weighted average: α*best + (1-α)*worst, and selects the highest.
coverage_criteria: Student can define the realism/Hurwicz criterion
Student can interpret the coefficient α as degree of optimism
Student can compute the weighted average for given α and identify optimal choice

candidates.label: Decision Environments
candidates.description: Four types of decision contexts: certainty (known outcomes), uncertainty (no probability information), risk (known probabilities), and conflict (adversarial decisions).
coverage_criteria: Student can list the four environments
Student can distinguish them based on knowledge of states and probabilities

candidates.label: Payoff Table as a Decision Tool
candidates.description: A table that organizes payoffs for each decision alternative under various states of nature, used as input to decision criteria.
coverage_criteria: Student can construct a payoff table given alternatives and states
Student can interpret payoffs from a table

candidates.label: Maximax Criterion (Optimistic)
candidates.description: Optimistic rule: choose the alternative with the maximum possible payoff (best of the best).
coverage_criteria: Student can identify the maximax choice from a payoff table
Student can explain its optimistic nature

candidates.label: Maximin Criterion (Pessimistic)
candidates.description: Pessimistic rule: choose the alternative with the best worst-case payoff (guarantee a minimum).
coverage_criteria: Student can determine the maximin choice from a payoff table
Student can explain its conservative philosophy

candidates.label: Minimax Regret Criterion
candidates.description: Minimize maximum regret: construct regret table, find worst regret for each alternative, choose the smallest worst regret.
coverage_criteria: Student can construct a regret table from payoffs
Student can compute minimax regret and select alternative

candidates.label: Expected Value Criterion (Decision under Risk)
candidates.description: When probabilities are known, compute expected monetary value for each alternative and choose the highest.
coverage_criteria: Student can assign given probabilities to states
Student can calculate expected payoffs
Student can determine optimal decision under risk

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
